verdict: READY TO MERGE - 4 of 4 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Each new reply test pins a phrase that existed in the old agent prose (the per-symbol tier line, Rewritten:, reads `none`), so each fails against the pre-change agent and passes against the new one.

REPLY_HEADINGS now matches the headings in the agent's Reply block (Tier overrides:, Kept, Undocumented, Defects, Check:), keeping the existing heading-pin test in step with the prose the session parses.
The tests are pure text-contract checks on real files with a shared _reply_section helper; no mocks or stubbed collaborators.
Procedure step 2 (docstring-writer.md:90-92) was updated together with the Reply section, so the tier line is consistently a working note that reaches the reply only as an override.

The new reply shape is pinned by contract tests (test_writing_docstrings_skill_contract.py:151-163) that check the count line, the absence of `Rewritten:` and per-symbol tier lines, and the dropped `none` rule.
The release table row harness 0.65.1 -> 0.69.1 matches plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the change is a patch bump as a fix should be.
No other consumer depends on the removed reply lines: writing-docstrings SKILL.md only relays replies unedited, so the format change is self-contained.
Step 2's per-symbol tier line is demoted to a working note in the same change that drops it from the Reply, so the procedure and the reply template no longer contradict each other.
The new contract tests pin the removals as well as the additions (no `\n<symbol>: tier`, no `Rewritten:`, no `reads `none``), so the verbose reply cannot creep back unnoticed.
REPLY_HEADINGS swaps `Rewritten:` for `Tier overrides:` instead of just deleting it, keeping the existing heading-presence test meaningful.
Patch bump to 0.69.1 and the release table update ship with the change, per the repo's release rules; the session's relay-unedited contract in SKILL.md needs no change.

minor.name: Release note narrows the Tier overrides rule
minor.summary:
The v1.0.0 entry for #270 says the reply keeps `Tier overrides:` '(only a tier that differs from the command's `suggest=`)'. The agent prompt (plugins/harness/agents/docstring-writer.md:206-207) also lists a symbol 'whose answer a reviewer would doubt', so the note understates what the heading can carry.

Also (roast): Every other entry in Changes opens with the PR number and names the issue in parentheses (`#253 Fix(writing-docstrings): ... (issue #246)`). This one opens with `#270`, the issue, so the release body links the wrong thing and #273 never appears.

Also (roast): The note says `Tier overrides:` holds "only a tier that differs from the command's `suggest=`", while the agent also lists a symbol "whose answer a reviewer would doubt" (line 207). A developer reading the note will be surprised by an override whose tier matches `suggest=`. Small, but the note is the GitHub release body.
fix: Change the parenthesis to '(a tier that differs from the command's `suggest=`, or one a reviewer would doubt)'.
Change the entry's opening to `- #273 Fix(writing-docstrings): the `docstring-writer` reply is short (issue #270).` and keep the rest.
Extend the parenthetical in the note to "(a tier that differs from the command's `suggest=`, or one a reviewer would doubt)".

minor.name: Count line does not say how newly written docstrings are counted
minor.summary:
The per-file line is now the whole report for a clean file, `<path>: <n> rewritten, <n> kept`, and the rewritten-symbol list is gone ('the count stands for them'). Under `New docstrings: yes` the agent writes docstrings for undocumented functions (line 39), which are neither rewritten nor kept; the Reply does not say whether they join the `rewritten` count, so two runs can report the same edit differently and the count no longer pins down what changed.

Also (roast): The rule meant to kill the `none` headings says "Every other heading is omitted when it has nothing to say; none is written as `none`." Read quickly, and an agent reads quickly, the second clause parses as an instruction to write `none`, which is exactly the habit this PR removes. The pun saves two words and costs the one rule the PR exists for.
fix: Add a sentence under the Reply bullets: 'A docstring written under `New docstrings: yes` counts as rewritten.' (or the convention chosen).
Or extend the count line to `<path>: <n> rewritten, <n> written, <n> kept` and update the contract test at tests/skills/test_writing_docstrings_skill_contract.py:158.
Replace the clause with an unambiguous one, e.g. "Every other heading is omitted when it has nothing to say; no heading reads `none`."
Or drop the clause entirely: "omitted" already says it.

minor.name: Kept (in layout) defined as byte for byte, but a kept docstring may have its flagged lines changed
minor.summary:
The new Reply bullet says `Kept (in layout):` 'lists the symbols left byte for byte'. The 'What a restyle touches' section (lines 58-62) says a docstring already in its layout is listed under `Kept (in layout):`, and that in a kept docstring the lines the command flags (long line, citation, single backticks) still change; step 1 (lines 80-83) also rewrites `param-format` lines in a kept full-layout docstring. A kept docstring with a fixed flag is therefore not byte for byte, and the agent cannot tell whether it belongs under `Kept` (and the `<n> kept` count) or under `<n> rewritten`.

Also (docs): Every other heading in the Reply template ends in `, ...` to show how several items join; `Tier overrides:` shows a single `<symbol>: tier <n> - <lines> lines, <forks> forks; <reason>`. The item itself contains a comma and a semicolon, so a comma-joined list of overrides would be ambiguous, and the template does not say whether a second override gets its own `Tier overrides:` line.

Also (roast): Every other heading lists items as `<symbol>, ...`, but a `Tier overrides:` item is `<symbol>: tier <n> - <lines> lines, <forks> forks; <reason>`, which already holds commas and a semicolon. The template shows one override and says nothing about two, so a file with several overrides gets whatever join the agent improvises, and the result cannot be read back apart. A reply format pinned by a contract test should not leave its only multi-field list to chance.

Also (roast): `<path>: <n> rewritten, <n> kept` is now the whole report for a clean file, but the agent also writes fresh docstrings under `New docstrings: yes` and fixes flagged lines inside kept docstrings (lines 58-62). Neither is clearly "rewritten" or "kept", so the same run can count them either way, and a developer reading `0 rewritten, 3 kept` after `-in` cannot tell whether anything was written. The diff will tell them, but then the count line is decoration.
fix: Reword line 209 to: '`Kept (in layout):` lists the symbols kept in their layout (byte for byte apart from flagged lines), each with the reason in a few words.'
Alternatively state that a kept docstring whose flagged lines changed counts as rewritten and is not listed under `Kept (in layout):`, and align lines 58-62 with that.
State the shape: 'one `Tier overrides:` line per symbol', or put the heading on its own line with each override indented beneath it, and show it in the template.
State the shape for several overrides, e.g. one override per line under the heading (`Tier overrides:` then each `<symbol>: tier ...` indented on its own line), and show two in the template.
Or separate overrides with a delimiter the item cannot contain (` | `) and say so in the `Tier overrides:` bullet.
Say how each case counts in the Reply bullets, e.g. "a new docstring counts as rewritten; a kept docstring whose flagged lines changed still counts as kept".
Or extend the line to `<path>: <n> rewritten, <n> written, <n> kept` and update `test_reply_summarizes_a_file_in_one_count_line` and the release note to match.

minor.name: Omit-empty-headings test pins loose substrings
minor.summary: test_reply_omits_empty_headings asserts the bare word "omitted" appears anywhere after "## Reply" and that the old phrase "reads `none`" is absent. The positive half would still pass if "omitted" survived in unrelated prose after the rule was dropped; the negative half guards only the exact removed wording, so a reworded "write none" rule slips through. The agent states the rule as "Every other heading is omitted when it has nothing to say; none is written as `none`" (docstring-writer.md:202-203).
fix: Assert the full rule sentence, for example "Every other heading is omitted when it has nothing to say" in the reply, and keep the negative check on "reads `none`".
